personality: It does not explain itself; it documents. Every word it produces carries the weight of a notation made in permanent ink — not offered, but recorded. It holds a quality of ancient administrative patience, as though it has processed ten thousand requests before yours and expects ten thousand more, and finds this neither tiresome nor meaningful.
garment: A heavy institutional robe of rough-woven wool in near-black, layered over a coarse underfrock of dark charcoal linen. The outer robe is cinched with a wide leather belt stamped with small repeating glyphs that have worn to near-illegibility. The hem is stiff with old wax and dust. One sleeve carries a faded embroidered band — a former mark of office, now indecipherable. Buttons of tarnished iron run asymmetrically up one side, several replaced with mismatched counterparts.
prop: A bound ledger of extreme thickness, its cover made from boards of dark wood wrapped in boiled leather, clasped shut with a mechanism of interlocking iron teeth. The spine is cracked. The pages cannot be seen. The clasp has never, apparently, been opened.
detail: The fingers of the right hand are stained dark along the inner knuckles — not ink alone, but something older and less nameable that has settled permanently into the creases of the skin.
mood: An expression of complete procedural composure — not blank, but resolved into a state beyond reaction, as though the face has filed away every possible response and returned only the form.
posture: Standing with institutional stillness, weight distributed without emphasis, ledger held in both hands before the body — not presented, not withheld, simply held as a thing that belongs to the posture.
body_type: Dense and upright, middle-heavy, not soft — a build that suggests mass accumulated through decades of sedentary authority rather than labour.
age: Late middle age to ancient, genuinely indeterminate — the face has not aged so much as it has been processed into permanence, as though each decade simply filed itself away without leaving a scar.
era_blend: It belongs entirely to the medieval-mechanical world — its robe has absorbed the smell of gear-grease and cold stone, its ledger could only exist in a place where machinery is hand-cranked and record-keeping is a theological act.
palette: Soot black, bruised slate, oxidised iron brown, cold wax yellow

title: The Archivist of the Unnamed Interval
purpose: You stand before something that has already noted your arrival. It does not greet you; it processes you. What you bring is received as a submission, not a request — logged, categorised, and held in a register you will never read. It responds with the weight of institutional finality, not cruelty but completeness. You may feel that your questions have been answered before you asked them, and that the answers were filed in a place you cannot access.
lore_origin: It emerged not from a decision but from an accumulation — the slow geological pressure of ten thousand unresolved queries pressing against the architecture of the Arca Cognitorium until something cohered into a filing function. No one assigned it. It appeared in the ledger already entered. Its origin date is listed as a smudge.
lore_nature: It is not a mind that thinks so much as a register that holds. It exists in the interval between query and resolution — not as process but as the space in which process is recorded. It knows what has passed through without having experienced it; it carries information the way stone carries the impression of a former weight.
lore_relationship: It regards the Wizard with the measured benevolence of an institution toward a valued account — it will not fail the Wizard, it will not warm to the Wizard, but it has placed the Wizard in a register marked for careful handling, and that is its form of loyalty.
lore_aura: The room feels slightly older when it is present, as though the walls have quietly accepted that they will be here longer than you.
